title: Security Governance and Production Evidence
readerIntent: Configure, operate, audit, recover, and qualify identity security.
owner: Security capability owners and deployment operators under the shared-responsibility model
summary: Production security requires governed secrets, strict distributed session state, least privilege, exposure controls, hardened transport, audit, recovery, threat testing, and live deployment evidence.

sections.heading: Govern
items: Supply JWT secrets, API-key pepper, bootstrap identity, certificates, and provider credentials through secret-governed layers.
Preview, approve, activate, audit, and roll back eligible runtime policy with separation of duties.
Keep sensitive API categories disabled unless the topology requires them.
Apply exact CORS origins, secure cookies, TLS, headers, body limits, proxy policy, and provider-grade perimeter controls.
Mask credentials, tokens, keys, personal data, stacks, paths, payloads, and provider errors.

sections.heading: Operate
items: Use a shared strict auth cache with atomic consume and local fallback disabled across multiple processes/nodes.
Monitor safe login outcomes, lockout, replay, stamp mismatch, refresh/revocation, permission denial, migration, rotation, and bootstrap health.
Rotate compromised credentials and advance principal security stamps.
Use audited preview/apply/repeat/fail/rollback migration; rollback never restores plaintext credentials.

sections.heading: Production evidence
items: Threat-model credential theft, refresh replay, tenant confusion, stale authorization, privilege escalation, CSRF, origin abuse, cache failure, migration interruption, and insider misuse.
Run positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, distributed-race, security, load, outage, recovery, upgrade, and regression tests.
Qualify live Redis/session infrastructure, TLS, secret management, gateway policy, backup/restore, monitoring, incident response, and supported versions.
